newsitem.title: POLAND: Debica sees 1997 profits well above 1996.
newsitem.headline: Debica sees 1997 profits well above 1996.

text.p: Polish tyre maker TC Debica SA expects its profits this year to well exceed its 1996 results, Debica's chief executive said on Friday.
"Debica will record in 1997 much better profits than in 1996," Zdzislaw Chabowski told a news conference.
He would not give exact forecasts.

In 1996 Debica made a pre-tax profit of 63 million zlotys and a net profit of 36.4 million zlotys on sales of 605.9 million. It earned net 19.5 million zlotys on sales of 164.9 million zlotys in the first quarter of this year.

Chabowski said that Debica, 50.7 percent owned by U.S. tyre company Goodyear & Rubber Co. and Poland's leader in the passenger-car tyre market, was keen to increase its share in all segments of the Polish market.

"We are hungry for success and any percent of market share in any given market segment, whether it is tyres for passenger cars, trucks, replacement or the original equipment market. All segments are important for us," he said.

Chabowski also said Debica would launch sales in Poland of a new German-made tyre for luxury passenger cars designed for high velocities and could launch its Polish production if demand proved sufficient.
